summary: A convincing medieval foundation: the four occupations are distinguishable, and the crown and motley identify King and jester immediately. Resolve visible hood interference, the Elder’s top-hat silhouette, and trouser-like robe construction before approval.
problems: The shorter Messenger has conspicuous horizontal striping across the hood opening, consistent with retained hair intersecting the hood.
The Market Elder’s upright cylindrical crown and narrow brim read as a top hat, suggesting the Industrial Age rather than an unmistakably medieval cap.
The King’s lower robe reads as two straight trouser legs. The Breadmaker and Elder also need stronger gown silhouettes without rigid geometry bridging their moving legs.

In this view, the caravan leader reads clearly as a jester but less clearly as a visitor from another court. The small heraldic details and rear travel bundle do little to establish that distinction at stream scale.
fix: Carpenter: Keep the short split tunic, waist apron, fallen cowl and broad mallet head; these distinguish the trade well. Give the cowl a consistent contrasting wool colour so it remains readable on both wearer palettes, and keep the mallet handle visibly seated in the hand. Breadmaker: Keep the coif, waist-only cream apron and chunky loaf. Add modest outward flare to each leg-bound gown panel, preserve clearance between the inner edges, and expose a clear shoe strip beneath the hem. Market Elder: Replace the stacked brim-and-cylinder hat with a low, broad, asymmetric soft cap or folded medieval bonnet. Retain the forked staff and mantle clasp; add leg-bound outer hem flare and ensure the green mantle contrasts with green shirts. Young Messenger: Add hair to hide, then fit the hood shell cleanly around both heads. Check the head-bound hood and cape-bound liripipe remain connected through head turns; preserve the strong dagged shoulder edge, satchel and tall boots. King: Keep the crown, blue-and-red palette and pale mantle collar. Broaden the robe toward its outer lower edges using separate leg-bound panels, add a substantial gold hem band, and avoid a rigid skirt spanning both legs. Make the sceptre shaft more visible beyond the fist so it reads as an office-bearing object rather than an isolated gold ball. Caravan leader: Preserve the excellent three-point cap and large ivory-blue divisions. Enlarge the split-diamond foreign-court badge onto a broad shoulder tab and repeat it on the travel pack; make the rolled bundle visible beside the upper torso from the gameplay camera. Keep this heraldry exclusive to the travelling court.
